# Film take: a take can hold at a named step for an introduction or explanatory shot

## Context

The film's A6 narration (#15252) opens with a hook over the window birth and then the team's introductions — the operator's steer of 2026-10-10 20:4xZ (via Emmy): "our self-intros and matching video/voice content are crucial; more content from us is optional". Emmy's measured bindings (20:55Z) put the introduction's picture between the verified birth and the journey (Continue released no earlier than birth + 20.95 s) and ask for a living-room explanatory interval after the native return (M06 + E02 = 8.4 s before the rail's pin). The take at PR #19570's head gives those passages ≈ 1 s each: the committed breath, then the journey's gate resolves at once; the whole-again beat, then the rail's pin.

Design authority: the operator's steer above, within the 2026-09-23 pacing rule (no gesture or pause stretched to fit a line) and the screenplay's own gate contract — "a gate is a wait, not pacing" (`WorkstationFilmTourNL` third test). An introduction or an explanation over the living room is a designed shot with its own content, not a stretched pause; the question is only where its time comes from, and the answer must leave the in-app viewer's tour and the headless witnesses untouched.

## The Problem

Under `autoGates` the controller's step settlement returns as soon as the cue and the refresh settle: replays and takes never wait anywhere. The two shots sit exactly at existing steps — the second gate's step (`film-journey[0]`, right after the committed birth) and the whole-again beat (`film-reintegration[2]`) — but the take cannot hold there. The alternatives are worse: cue-free `pause`s of 19 s and 8 s in the screenplay break the 1.5 s reading-beat bound that `fiveBeatFilm.spec` pins and make every in-app viewer wait; a viewer-mode gate in the take renders the Continue button into the recording (`TourToolbar`'s `workstation-tour-continue`, bound to `tour.gatePrompt`) and the return has no gate at all.

## The Architectural Reality

- `apps/workstation/view/TourController.mjs`: `autoGates` is a plain field set through `startTour({autoGates})` / `runVisibleTour` or directly before Start by a transport; `settleTourStep(data)` is the host's settlement barrier the runner awaits per step (`TourRunner` → `stepSettlement`), awaiting the step's cue settlement and the workspace refresh — a cue that failed throws there. The controller extends `Neo.controller.Component` → `core.Base#timeout(time, {signal})` is the destroy-safe wait (registered-async contract; rejects with `Neo.isDestroyed`).
- The tour receipt (`getTourReceipt`) is the cue clock the take's QA reads, so a hold must appear in it.
- `test/playwright/unit/apps/workstation/TourController.spec.mjs` pins the gate contract; the film witness asserts both gates `continued: 'auto'` under autoGates and that no gate ever waited for a viewer. The controller's own progress path (`onTourStepSettled`) awaits a 90 ms `timeout` per step, so a wall-clock floor on a whole playback cannot prove that a hold ran (Sophie's falsifier on PR #19572, review 5480839549).
- The scratch take runner (host-local, never committed) sets `{autoGates: true}` through the Neural Link before pressing Start.

## The Fix

In `TourController`: a plain field `takeHoldMs` (default `null`; `{'<sceneId>[<stepIndex>]': ms}`, a `startTour`/`runVisibleTour` option like `autoGates`). In `settleTourStep`, after the step's own barrier (cue settlement + refresh, unchanged), under `autoGates` only: the hold the key names → `this.timeout(hold)`, recorded as `{heldMs, sceneId, stepIndex}` in `holds`, which the tour receipt carries (reset per playback). No prompt is published, so no Continue button renders; the viewer's tour (no `autoGates`) reads no hold. The take runner passes `takeHoldMs: {'film-journey[0]': <intro>, 'film-reintegration[2]': <return>}`; the headless witnesses pass nothing and keep their receipts unchanged. (The first cut of this ticket keyed the hold to gate ordinals; Emmy's return interval showed the hold belongs to any named step — corrected in place, 21:0xZ.)

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TourController.takeHoldMs` — plain field; `startTour(script, {takeHoldMs})` / `runVisibleTour(script, {takeHoldMs})` option; settable directly before Start by a transport (`setProperties` over the Neural Link) | `apps/workstation/view/TourController.mjs` (`takeHoldMs`, `runVisibleTour`, `settleTourStep`) | Shape `{'<sceneId>[<stepIndex>]': ms}`; a key names a step by the screenplay's scene id and the step's index within that scene. A finite `ms > 0` holds; `0`, negative or missing keys hold nothing. The option **omitted** keeps the current map (same contract as `autoGates`); `null` clears every hold. Read only while `autoGates` is true: viewer mode (`autoGates: false`) never holds, whatever the map holds. | Default `null`: no hold anywhere — the in-app tour and the headless witnesses | The field's and both methods' JSDoc | `TourController.spec`: the take-hold test (the hold blocks the next beat until release; viewer mode records none; the map survives into the next playback); `WorkstationFilmTourNL` 3/3 + `WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL` 5/5 with the default |
| The hold's place in the settlement barrier | `settleTourStep` | The hold runs AFTER the step's own barrier: a failed cue still throws before any hold (`cueFailed`), the workspace refresh still settles first; the wait is `core.Base#timeout`, so destroying or cancelling the controller mid-hold rejects with `Neo.isDestroyed` and the existing cancel/cleanup path runs — a hold can never mask a failure or outlive its owner | n/a (no hold → the barrier is unchanged) | `settleTourStep` JSDoc + inline note | `TourController.spec`: "a failed window cue fails its beat…", the cancellation tests (unchanged), the take-hold test's stubbed `timeout` |
| `getTourReceipt().holds` | `TourController` receipt assembly (`runVisibleTour`) | `[{heldMs, sceneId, stepIndex}]` in settlement order, one entry per hold that completed. **`heldMs` is the REQUESTED (configured) duration, not a measurement** — the measured picture time is the take's beat log and the receipt's `elapsedMs`. Reset to `[]` at each playback start (`runVisibleTour`); `[]` when no hold ran | `[]` | The `holds` member's JSDoc | `TourController.spec` take-hold test (`holds` equals the configured entries; a second playback records afresh); the next take's receipt (AC-3, #15252) |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `TourController.spec`: under `autoGates` with `takeHoldMs = {'s[0]': <ms>}` the gate still settles synchronously and prompt-free, the next beat cannot start until the hold's wait is released (a controllable hold, isolated from the controller's progress waits — a wait replaced by an already-resolved promise fails the test), the receipt's `holds` records `{heldMs, sceneId, stepIndex}` afresh per playback; with `autoGates: false` the same configuration records no hold.
- [ ] The film tour witness and the popup-overlap witness stay green with the default (no hold); the gate receipts are unchanged.
- [ ] Post-merge: the next take at the merged head holds `film-journey[0]` for the introduction shot and `film-reintegration[2]` for the explanation (Emmy's bindings set the values) and its receipt's `holds` shows both (#15252).

## Out of Scope

- The portrait cards, the explanatory overlay and the CTA card (the cut; #15252).
- The recorder's post-roll for the closing lines (take runner only, no app change).
- Any screenplay change: the steps' positions, captions and pauses stay as they are.
